newsitem.title: UK: UK budget shows Labour more than 1-term govt - Brown.
newsitem.headline: UK budget shows Labour more than 1-term govt - Brown.

text.p: The long-term nature of last week's budget shows the new Labour government has its eyes firmly fixed on more than one term in office, Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said on Friday.
In a speech to the Young Labour conference in Bournemouth, Brown said the budget was not about fine-tuning or quick fixes but about the long-term needs of Britain's economy.
"This will not be a one-term government. This is a government for the long term, addressing the long-term challenges we face with long-term solutions," Brown said.
Excerpts of his speech were released in London.
"The ultimate judgement on the decisions we take now will not be made this week, this month or even this year but next year and in the years ahead," Brown said.
He said the measures contained in the budget and the decisions he had taken since coming to office aimed to deliver on four long-term priorities:
-- achieving stability in monetary and fiscal policy, keeping inflation low and the public finances in order.
-- investment to equip the economy for the future.
-- educational, employment and economic opportunity for all.
Brown said Labour had honoured its promises since the election -- for example by imposing a windfall tax on utilities and cutting VAT on fuel -- and would continue to do so.
